summary: Legacy-username SSO device claim truncation causes 403 on SSH gateway impersonation
description:
Issue summary:
Several users with legacy usernames (containing a dot + suffix, e.g. 'j.smith+team') intermittently receive a 403 when attempting to SSH through the company SSH gateway. The gateway validates Okta SSO assertions including a device_claim (device_id/device_fingerprint) injected by our Device Trust pipeline. The identity-proxy is truncating the device_claim under certain lengths, causing downstream service-side assertion mismatch and immediate 403 / impersonation failure.

Impact:
- A subset of internal employees cannot establish SSH sessions via the centralized SSH gateway (affects ~12 users reported in past 48h).
- Blocks oncall and incident runbook access for those users.
- No production workloads impacted beyond internal tooling access, but this is high-priority because it affects incident response.

Environment:
- production cluster behind identity-proxy v1.12.3 (us-west region)
- Okta Device Trust enforcement enabled for SSH gateway app

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use a test account with a legacy username pattern (e.g. j.smith+infra@example.com) that has device-trust enrolled.
2) Initiate SSH through the centralized ssh-gateway which redirects to Okta SSO device flow.
3) Complete device attestation and allow SSO redirect back to identity-proxy.
4) Observe gateway returns 403 and session is not established.

Observed logs / evidence:
- identity-proxy stderr (excerpt):
  [2026-03-12T08:23:12Z] WARN auth: incoming assertion device_claim length 520, truncating to 256
  [2026-03-12T08:23:12Z] ERROR ssh-gateway: user "j.smith+infra" assertion mismatch after device_claim rewrite -> 403
- Okta auth audit (correlated):
  2026-03-12T08:23:11Z  AUTH_SUCCESS user=j.smith+infra app=ssh-gateway claims_total=7 device_claim_len=520
- Browser/CLI symptom: immediate "Permission denied (publickey)" followed by gateway 403 in support logs.

Investigation notes:
- Triage by oncall identity-engineer (Diego M.) confirmed truncation happens in the identity-proxy component when claim length >256 bytes; this is new behavior after the 2026-03-10 hotfix to sanitize incoming headers (PR: https://github.com/redwood/identity-proxy/pull/405).
- Reproduced locally by forging SAML assertion with long device_claim; identity-proxy drops trailing bytes and emits a WARN. Downstream SSH gateway performs an exact-compare on the device_claim and denies when mismatch occurs.
- Hypothesis: previous token pipeline normalized username + device claim ordering; the new sanitizer trims header values at 256 bytes which wasn't an issue for non-legacy usernames. Legacy usernames produce longer combined claims due to appended '+' suffix and device metadata.
- Quick check shows no Okta-side truncation; Okta advertises device_claim up to ~1k bytes in our tenant.
- Session cookies for affected users show regenerated session IDs after the failed flow, suggesting identity-proxy rejects upstream assertion before session finalization.

Comments:
- "Diego Marquez (Identity): I've reproduced the truncation locally and confirmed the identity-proxy sanitizer enforces a 256-byte header cap. Working on a patch to allow 1k bytes for device_claim only. Will open PR for review." 2026-03-12T14:02Z
- "SRE oncall (Marta Chen): Confirmed two oncall users were impacted during incident window; provided per-user workarounds (clear cookies + use web-based ssh-console which uses alternate flow)." 2026-03-13T09:30Z
- "Support (Aisha): Collected 12 affected usernames, sample assertion payloads, and keyed linked incidents. Adding to ticket." 2026-03-13T11:45Z

Action items / tentative fix plan:
- Short term workaround: instruct affected users to clear identity-proxy cookies and use the web-console ssh fallback or use a temporary service account to escalate. Documented in the incident Slack thread #support-ssh.
- Code change: update identity-proxy sanitizer to allow device_claim header up to 1024 bytes and only apply relaxed cap to header name 'X-Device-Claim' to avoid wide-open header size increases. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/identity-proxy/pull/418 (draft).
- Add normalization step in auth pipeline to canonicalize legacy usernames (strip '+' suffixes for device-claim generation) to avoid oversized combined claim metadata.
- Add automated regression test to identity-proxy for device_claim sizes and for legacy username patterns.

Resolution / current status:
- Workaround shared with affected users.
- Draft fix PR created and assigned to Diego for tests and CI adjustments.
- Planned deploy to staging: 2026-03-15; canary to prod-us-west 2026-03-17 if tests pass.
- Follow-up: add monitoring alert when identity-proxy emits more than 5 "truncating" WARNs in 10m for device_claim in production.

Follow-up notes:
- Link to related incident postmortem will be added after production rollout.
- Consider long-term: reconcile device metadata format with Okta Device Trust team to prevent oversized claims and add server-side resilient comparison (hash compare instead of raw-compare).

notes_for_runbook: If new reports arrive: 1) collect assertion via identity-proxy logs (enable debug for request-id) 2) ask user to clear cookies and retry via web-console 3) if still failing, use temporary service account to escalate, attach logs to ticket and notify identity-engineering oncall.
